newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bonds sell in line with U.S., mkt awaits data.
newsitem.headline: NZ bonds sell in line with U.S., mkt awaits data.

text.p: New Zealand bonds sold off slightly at Thursday's open, as a nervous U.S. Treasury market weakened amid renewed fears the Federal Reserve will hike rates again at its next policy setting meeting in early May.
The mid bonds were up three basis points in yield to 7.86 percent while the 11/06 maturity was up four to 8.07 percent. Dealers said flows were relatively light following the rally of recent days.
The money market was equally quiet as dealers awaited December quarter current account data at 10.45 a.m. (2245 GMT).

A Reuters poll of 13 economists showed an average expectation of a NZ$1.13 billion deficit in the quarter and a 4.25 billion annual deficit. The September quarter deficit was $2.17 billion ($4.20 billion annual deficit).

"People are watching it, but it will be a currency-led day if there is a move off the current account data, because of the recent talk about it (the deficit) blowing out," one money market dealer said.

"It will be more a sentiment factor for the currency than anything else. If the currency moves we are -- in the short end at least -- so tied in to the TWI levels at the moment that it will determine the direction on the day."
Ahead of the data the 90-day bank bills were flat at 7.40 percent but dealers said the price action had been slightly defensive following Tuesday's sharp rally on the back of muted inflation figures.
The June futures contract was a point weaker at 92.48, with 647 contracts traded.
